When we think about tokimeki, there are 3 main circles that you should try to keep in balance to make joy more sustainable in your life. They are：

1. Your Joy Circle: Understanding Your Joy
Finding joy for yourself is essential. It is what drives you forward. When you are fulfilled and happy, your capacity to contribute increases, and when self-care becomes possible, it becomes easier to thrive and share.

2. Your Social Circle: To Share & Amplify
Joy multiplies when shared. Understanding what sparks joy for those you care about creates stronger bonds and mutual support. When you have social joy, even personal achievements can feel more exciting.

3. Your Value Circle: What You Bring Beyond Yourself. What You Bring to the World
Through work, art, service, or innovation, contribute to the world. With external value, the practice can become much more sustainable as a lifestyle.

Your personal joy circle, your social circle, and your value circle.
All three together to create a more joyful life for you, your people, and the world.

✨Follow us as we share practices, rituals, prompts, etc. to learn how!

Being able to trust your intuition and act on what sparks joy takes real courage.

So often, we second-guess ourselves. We wonder whether our instincts are right, whether we should choose the practical path, or whether what lights us up is worth pursuing at all.

But Tokimeki begins when we start listening to that inner spark and trusting it, one small decision at a time. We don't need to make dramatic changes overnight. Even the smallest shifts toward what brings us joy can lead us toward a more meaningful and fulfilling life.

Comment a ❤️ if you're committing to the process of finding your Tokimeki and following it!

#tokimeki #artiftokimeki #personaldevelopment #personaljourney #sparkjoy

“Every time I tidy up, my baby pulls everything back out… I can’t even have a tidying festival!”
I receive many comments similar to this from parents with young children, and I completely understand!
When my children were babies, they would also pull placemats from drawers, knock over things like salt bags, and turn organized spaces into chaos!
So, what did I do?
I made the baby playpen my ally, using those quiet moments to tidy whatever I could, even if it was only for a few minutes.
I also created a “mess is OK” drawer in the kitchen where my children could safely explore and pull things out.
But most importantly, I learned that you can tidy in small increments.
“Today, I’ll just tackle the pens.”
“Today, I’ll just organize the mugs.”
That is enough.
The KonMari Method encourages tidying by category, but the way you tidy can and should adapt to your stage of life.
If you’re raising young children, embrace a bite-sized approach. Use those little pockets of time when you can, adapt the method to fit your life, and give yourself permission to say, “This is enough for today.”
One small step at a time✨

Tokimeki sensitivity isn't something you're simply born with. It's a skill you can gently develop over time👇✨

The more often you pause to notice what genuinely sparks joy, the more sensitive you become to it.

Over time, that sensitivity begins to guide your everyday life. You notice more, you appreciate more, and the decisions that once felt uncertain start to feel surprisingly intuitive.

Not because you've changed who you are, but because you've become better at listening to yourself.

📌 Join us as we explore the Art of Tokimeki with weekly reflections, practical guides, and inspiration to help you cultivate a life that feels uniquely joyful.
